clues: This town sits in the south part of a state split by great lakes. It stands where a big river and a small river meet.
Winters here are cold, with moderate to heavy snow. Summers turn very warm and humid, and snow can fall from November to April.
In 1847, the state moved its capital to this small new town. The old port town sat too close to a foe's land, so they chose a safe spot inland.
Cars put this town on the map of the world. Its shops built cars by the thousands, year after year.
The governor of Michigan works in this city. State lawmakers meet here, in the middle of the state.
